sections.label: Singapore seniors and dementia numbers
sections.summary: Around one in six Singaporeans is 65 or older, and dementia cases are projected to rise from 92,000 to 152,000 in eight years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, around one in six Singaporeans is aged 65 and older, with an average lifespan of 83.5 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 2030, around one in four citizens will be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Amongst the seniors, one in 10 persons above age 60 has been diagnosed with dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At present, there are approximately 92,000 persons diagnosed with dementia and this number is projected to increase by 65% to 152,000 in the next eight years.

sections.label: Polyclinics by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, there will be 32 polyclinics island wide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 2030, there will be 32 polyclinics island wide.

sections.label: Nursing home capacity and waiting times
sections.summary: Nursing home waiting time is nine months to a year, and bed capacity will rise to more than 31,000 in 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that the rate of increase may not keep up with the needs of the growing number of PLWDs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I understand that the current waiting time for nursing homes is nine months to a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While I am heartened to note that in the next 10 years, our nursing home bed capacity will go up by close to another 100% to more than 31,000 beds, I am worried if this is even enough, especially for elderly with issues like dementia.

sections.label: Funding for dementia VWOs
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOH reviews the funding model for VWOs supporting dementia-friendly programmes so they can focus on services instead of fund-raising.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: After all, funds are required for these VWOs to scale up their services and do outreach so that more PLWDs and families can benefit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope that MOH can review the funding model for such VWOs supporting dementia-friendly programmes so that they can focus their energies and resources on their programmes and services instead of on organising fund-raising activities.

sections.label: SMRT Go-To-Points at stations
sections.summary: SMRT is providing 98 train stations with Go-To-Points by end-2022, where disoriented commuters can wait for family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For instance, SMRT is taking the lead to provide 98 of its train stations across Singapore with Go-To-Points by the end of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These Go-To-Points will allow disoriented customers or commuters to calm down and wait in a comfortable space for their family members to bring them home safely.

sections.label: Support for young onset dementia
sections.summary: The speaker requests more support for people with young onset dementia to promote inclusiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To promote inclusiveness, I would like to request more support for people with young onset dementia, or YOD.

sections.label: Dementia prevention and healthy lifestyle
sections.summary: A speaker asks if Singapore has more dementia than other developed countries and notes international studies show healthy habits can prevent or delay dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It leads me to wonder – does Singapore have a higher proportion of people with dementia, compared to other developed countries?

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note the launch of the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine Dementia Research Centre in April 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Evidence from various international studies shows that dementia can actually be prevented or delayed through the adoption of healthy lifestyle habits, including having regular physical activities, maintaining a balanced diet, not having excessive alcohol intake and not smoking.

sections.label: More resources for public health education
sections.summary: The Government should consider investing more in public education and campaigns and redesigning policies to nudge people to take greater responsibility for their own health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In addition to the initiatives in Healthier SG, the Government should consider investing more resources into public education and campaigns and to redesign policies and systems to nudge our people to take greater responsibility for their own health and self-care.

sections.label: Dementia as fast-growing national issue
sections.summary: The passage states that as a nation, dementia must be recognised as a fast-growing issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As a nation, we need to recognise dementia is a fast-growing issue.

sections.label: MOH three-pronged dementia approach
sections.summary: MOH adopts a three-pronged approach to dementia: strengthening prevention and early detection, building care service capacity, and enhancing caregiver support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MOH adopts a three-pronged approach to address dementia: first, strengthening prevention and early detection; second, building capacity of care services; and third, enhancing support for caregivers.

sections.label: Lancet Commission preventable dementia estimate
sections.summary: A 2020 Lancet Commission report estimated 40% of dementia cases can be prevented or delayed by addressing 12 modifiable risk factors including diabetes, obesity and hearing loss.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A 2020 report by the Lancet Commission estimated that 40% of dementia cases can be prevented or delayed by addressing 12 modifiable risk factors, including diabetes, obesity and hearing loss.

sections.label: Number of CREST Teams
sections.summary: As of December 2021, there are 68 CREST Teams.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As of December 2021, we have 68 CREST Teams.

sections.label: Dementia Day Care capacity
sections.summary: Dementia Day Care services provide custodial care, cognitive activities and reminiscence therapy, with capacity tripled from 1,000 places in 2015 to 4,200 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Dementia Day Care (DDC) services provide custodial care, cognitive stimulating activities and reminiscence therapy to improve or maintain the seniors' well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have more than tripled the capacity of DDCs from 1,000 places in 2015 to 4,200 places in 2021.

sections.label: Registered geriatricians and psychiatrists
sections.summary: As at December 2021, 152 geriatricians and 277 psychiatrists are registered with the Singapore Medical Council.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As at December 2021, there are 152 geriatricians and 277 psychiatrists registered with the Singapore Medical Council (SMC).

sections.label: Caregiver post-diagnosis support
sections.summary: The CREST-Post Diagnostic Support pilot reaches out to families upon diagnosis, with two teams as of December 2021, and the Caregivers Training Grant provides a $200 annual subsidy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Upon diagnosis, the caregiver may not fully understand the condition or know where to seek help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have, therefore, started the CREST-Post Diagnostic Support (PDS) pilot to proactively reach out to families upon diagnosis, link them up with resources and equip caregivers with coping strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As of December 2021, there are two CREST-PDS teams and we plan to expand the number in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Caregivers Training Grant (CTG) provides a $200 annual subsidy for attending courses, including on dementia care, where caregivers can learn to better manage their own stress and well-being.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs
sections.summary: A new set of Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs will be introduced by 2024 requiring employers to fairly consider and respond to employees' FWA requests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A new set of Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs will be further introduced by 2024 that will require employers to put in place a proper process to fairly consider and respond to employees' request for FWAs.

sections.label: Dementia Friendly Communities established
sections.summary: The initiative was well-received and 15 DFCs have since been established across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The initiative was well-received and we have since established 15 DFCs across Singapore.
